notes: Every other lexicon in this directory indexes on dissatisfaction. This one is deliberately different:
it looks for neutral-to-positive task-type words that, independent of any frustration signal, tend to
mark a bounded, well-defined, and often-repeated request (the kind of turn that is usually followed by
the user's own explanation of scope and a clear agent summary once the work is done).
'audit' is the prototype: when a user asks for one, the surrounding prompt and the follow-on summary
are frequently specific enough to justify packaging the request as a reusable skill.
The weight is intentionally the lowest in this lexicon set: a bare match here is a much weaker lead
than a frustration signal, but still worth a review pass.
The audit reports matches as leads for review, not as a claim that every matched turn is skill-worthy.

structured_task_request.description: Neutral-or-positive task-type words that name a bounded, well-defined, often-repeated kind of request, similar in kind to 'audit'.
